candidates.label: Miletus archaeological site
candidates.support: The extensively excavated site near modern Balat, south of the Meander river's mouth, is undisputed as ancient Miletus; the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's coordinate for the site and Wikidata's coordinate agree closely.

summary.text: Miletus was, per Livius.org, effectively the leading city among the Ionian Greeks, a major port south of Ephesus and, in earlier centuries, a center of Greek philosophy and colonization. On his third missionary journey Paul sailed past Ephesus to save time (Acts 20:16) and instead summoned the Ephesian elders to meet him at Miletus, where he delivered the farewell address recorded beginning at Acts 20:18; Paul's second letter to Timothy also mentions leaving a companion sick at Miletus.

scripture.textWEB: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.
From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
Erastus remained at Corinth, but I left Trophimus at Miletus sick.
